div.head: Had 2[as Að]
div.ab: Mæssepreostes að 7 woruldþegenes is on Engla lage geteald efen dyre; 7 for þam seofon cyrichadan, þe se mæssepreost þurh Godes gife geþeah, þæt he hæfde, he bið þegenrihtes wyrþe.

Misse presbiteri et secularis thaini iusiurandum in Anglorum lege computatur (reputatur) eque carum; et pro septem ordinibus ecclesię, quo sacerdos per Dei donum ascendit, ut haberet, thaini recto (rectitudine) dignus est.
Be gehadodra manna aðe; 7 be hadbote. Mæssepreostes að 7 worldþegnes is on Engla lage geteald efen dire for ðam seofon cirichadan, þe se preost þurh Godes gife geþéah, þæt he hæfde.

Concerning the oath of ecclesiastics and concerning the compensation for offences against [those in] holy orders. The oath of a mass-priest and a secular thegn is in the law of the English reckoned equally valuable, because of the seven orders of the Church which the priest, prospering through the grace of God, has obtained.
A mass-priest's oath and a secular thegn's are considered equal in English law because of the seven Church degrees that the mass-priest has acquired through the grace of God

(Vom Eide geweihter Männer; und von Clerusbusse DO) Der Eid eines Priesters und [der] eines weltlichen Thegn wird im Engländer-Recht gleich [beurtheilt Ld] werthvoll gerechnet wegen der 7 kirchlichen Weihen [Ordines, die der P. emporsteigt lq], die zu erhalten der Priester durch Gottes Gnade das Glück hatte (gerechnet; und wegen — hatte, ist er Thegn-Privilegs würdig [gewürdigt Ld] hlq).

(Of the oath of ordained men; and of compensation for clergy, DO) The oath of a mass-priest and [that] of a secular thegn is reckoned equally valuable in English law, on account of the 7 church orders [through which the priest rises, lq] which the priest by God's grace was fortunate enough to receive (reckoned; and on account of … had, he is worthy [deemed worthy, Ld] of thegn-right, hlq).
div.note: This row is Að 2, not Hadbot: the sheet labels it ‘Had. 2 [as Að]’. In H it stands before Að 1. D and O's heading refers to Hadbot; it already stood in the exemplar of D and O and makes Had, which followed Að in the archetype of all MSS, a continuation of Að. ‘⁊ … wyrþe’ in H is as in Ld and the Quadripartitus.
